reconcile.note: Gill distinguishes Paul's justification before God in Romans 4:2 from James's justification before men in James 2:21, treating works as evidence, not cause.

discrepancy.note: Troki names it a contradiction: James's Abraham justified by works stands against Paul's insistence on justification by faith apart from works.

quotes.text: The opinion here cited meets with the contradiction of Paul, who writes in his Epistle to the Romans, chap, iii. 19,… Again, he says, in the same chapter, ver. 28, " Therefore, we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.''''
quotes.attr: Isaac ben Abraham Troki (d. 1594), Faith Strengthened (Chizzuk Emunah) (trans. Mocatta, 1851), ch. XCIII, on Romans 4:2 and James 2:21.

sides.snippet: For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about, but not toward God.
sides.verseText: For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about, but not toward God.

sides.snippet: Wasn't Abraham our father justified by works, in that he offered up Isaac his son on the altar?
sides.verseText: Wasn't Abraham our father justified by works, in that he offered up Isaac his son on the altar?
